title: Texas Woman's University (TWU)
summary: Texas Woman's University (TWU) is a university in Denton. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with TWU.

sections.heading: What TWU is known for
paragraphs: Texas Woman's University (TWU) is a public institution recognized for its strong emphasis on health-related programs, which constitute approximately 31.4% of its academic offerings. The university also maintains a significant focus on business education, with about 11.02% of its programs dedicated to this field. TWU serves a diverse undergraduate population of 8,767 students and has an admission rate of 96.12%, reflecting its inclusive enrollment approach. These characteristics highlight TWU's commitment to providing accessible education with particular strengths in health and business disciplines.

sections.heading: How to read TWU tuition
paragraphs: Texas Woman's University (TWU) tuition varies based on residency status. In-state students pay $8,640 annually for tuition, while out-of-state students are charged $18,480. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition, fees, and other expenses, amounts to $22,234. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and their families plan for the financial commitment associated with attending TWU.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Texas Woman's University (TWU) offers financial aid to support students in managing educational expenses. Approximately 42.01% of TWU students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies aimed at assisting low-income students. Among those who complete their programs, the median debt is $19,218, reflecting the typical borrowing amount upon graduation. Prospective students can explore detailed financial aid information and use the net price calculator available on TWU's official website at www.twu.edu/. Additional data can also be accessed through the College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?229179, providing transparency about costs and aid.

sections.heading: Denton and the TWU campus
paragraphs: Texas Woman's University (TWU) is located in Denton, Texas, within the 76204 zip code area. Denton is a city in the northern part of the state, known for its vibrant cultural scene and historic downtown. The TWU campus benefits from its position in Denton by providing students with access to various community resources and events. As part of the Dallas-Fort Worth metropolitan area, Denton offers a blend of urban amenities and a smaller city atmosphere, making it a distinctive setting for higher education.

paragraphs: Texas Woman's University (TWU) has a completion rate of approximately 49.06% within 150% of the expected time to graduate. sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Texas Woman's University (TWU) has a predominantly female student body, with women comprising approximately 91.79% of the population, while men represent about 8.21%. The university's racial and ethnic composition includes roughly 25.64% White, 17.68% Black, 40.77% Hispanic, and 8.83% Asian students. This diverse demographic reflects TWU's commitment to serving a broad spectrum of communities. Additionally, about 42.01% of students receive Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of the student body benefits from federal financial aid aimed at supporting low-income individuals.
